summary: How the Tapo app renames a camera (Device info > Name). The app trims the text, checks 1..32 UTF-8 bytes, and sends ONE camera command, setDeviceAlias {system:{sys:{dev_alias}}}, wrapped in multipleRequest through the camera's normal transport (LAN, or IoT cloud passthrough when away). There is no separate cloud alias/nickname call: on success the app only updates its in-memory caches and fires a local 'device list changed' tick. fc0.c0.J (the second half of the save) only renames NVR channels and is a no-op for stand-alone cameras.

items.description: Name rules of the app: the text is trimmed; it must be 1..32 bytes in UTF-8 (h2: getBytes("UTF-8").length > 0 && <= 32; f134487a = 32); the editor refuses input that would exceed 32 bytes and pre-fills the current name cut to 32 bytes (u1.J). Save is enabled only when the text is non-empty and differs from the current name. No character regex exists in code; a name the camera or app rejects is reported as error -63103 DEVICE_NAME_EXCESSIVE, shown as R.string.device_setting_device_name_len_error (log 'Incorrect alias format'); any other error shows general_failed.

items.description: Shared cameras: DeviceDetailInfoViewModelV2 marks a camera shared to the user (isUserRoleTypeDevice) whose auth type is neither OWNER nor ADVANCED as 'no permission'; the device-info page then shows camera_share_tip_no_permission instead of opening settings. This app therefore never sends setDeviceAlias for shared cameras (role != 0) and renames them only locally.

unresolved.detail: The app never updates the cloud itself; the cloud device list / thing nickname is expected to follow the camera's own report. How fast the cloud reflects a new dev_alias is not in the APK; this app keeps a pending local name until the cloud alias matches or 24 h pass.

The camera's own error code for a refused dev_alias (too long / bad characters) is not named in the APK; the app maps its own pre-check to -63103. This app reports any setDeviceAlias failure with the camera's code.
